page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance type within the N2 family, configured with a high ratio of virtual processing cores to system memory. Built on x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this server delivers 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores via multithreading. The CPU subsystem features a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI. It includes 64.0 GB of memory, allocating exactly 1.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration contains no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid multi-threaded performance and strong uncached memory bandwidth. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 211.46 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 92.34 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the upper performance tier. PassMark database operations also place in the upper tier with a score of 22021.79. In contrast, single-thread stress-ng throughput (1411.19) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.8 GB/sec) test in the lower quartile, whereas overall multi-core compute metrics across PassMark (45662.19) and Geekbench (12016.0) perform around the median.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio presents distinct architectural tradeoffs. The server provides substantial thread density for parallel workloads, but its constrained 64.0 GB memory envelope limits utilization for in-memory databases or dense cache stores. Consequently, the n2-highcpu-64 is best suited for horizontally scaled compute jobs, distributed build systems, Clang compilation pipelines, batch media processing, and high-concurrency microservices that require massive thread concurrency without large working memory footprints.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-64 is an Intel Xeon-powered instance configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores and 64.0 GB of system memory. Operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it features AVX-512 vector support and a 33 MB L3 cache. The machine comes with no bundled local storage, no discrete GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote block storage for persistent data. Hardware benchmarks reveal strong large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 211 GB/sec for reads and robust PassMark database performance, while single-threaded processing remains modest. With an allocation of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance type delivers cost-effective compute density for thread-heavy applications, multi-core compilation tasks, static web serving, and parallel batch workloads that operate within lean memory boundaries.
